exercises.prompt: What is a person's character, as against a self he is handed?

choices.text: The self he builds by his choices
An innate essence issued to him at birth
A stamp pressed on by other people, with no choice of his
Whatever mood he happens to be in at the moment

feedback.note: Character is the self he builds by his choices, not a finished self he is handed. An innate essence fails because the policy was formed, a social stamp fails because other people do not write his choices, and a mood fails because a passing feeling is not the self those choices make.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, this is just how I am, so I never chose it. What has he omitted?

choices.text: That other people own the self and may rename it
The choices that built the policy he now calls his nature
That character is only a mood, so there was nothing stable to choose
That saying the opposite would rewrite what he has in fact done

feedback.note: He has omitted the choices that built the policy now called how he is. A formed character is a fact, and it has a chosen history. Other people's ownership fails because they did not author the policy, a mood fails because the policy is stable, and a new announcement does not rewrite the history.

exercises.prompt: Is a formed character unreal because it was made by choice?

choices.text: Yes. Only what was never chosen can be a fact about a person
Yes. A self is real only when other people stamp it
No. It is a fact about him now. Choice explains its origin and does not erase it
No, because it was innate and the appearance of choice is the illusion

feedback.note: A formed character is a fact about the person now. Its origin in choice does not make it unreal, and its reality does not make it unchosen. Innateness fails because the policy was built. A social stamp fails because the choices were his. Unreality would follow only if choice could not produce facts, which it can.

exercises.prompt: Match each account of the self to the verdict it deserves.

pairs.right: What character is
Not the origin of that self
Not a substitute for his choices
A real fact with a chosen history

feedback.note: Character is the self one builds, and a formed character is a real fact with a chosen history. An innate essence and a social stamp both deny that origin. The fact is not a prison, because further choice can change a policy. It is also not a fiction merely because it was chosen.

exercises.prompt: Someone praises a virtue and adds that it was fated, so the person earns no credit. What is the error?

choices.text: Determinism. The virtue was built by his choices, so the achievement is his
The error is praising any virtue
Credit belongs to an instinct that selected the virtue before he acted
A group mind performed the virtue and lent him the name

feedback.note: The error is determinism. A virtue that was built by repeated choices is his achievement, so fate cannot be the author. Refusing praise fails because the achievement is real. An instinct fails because he has no innate code that selected it, and a group mind fails because only he made the choices.

exercises.prompt: A doctrine says a new neighborhood will replace his character without any choice of his. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: Character is innate, so a neighborhood is irrelevant for that different reason
The self is a whim, with no stability from one week to the next
Nothing is wrong. Other people are the mind that writes his policies
Circumstances can change what he faces. They do not write the self. Further choice changes a policy

feedback.note: Circumstances change what he faces, and they do not stamp a new character onto him, because a policy changes by his further choices. Innateness is the wrong correction, because the old policy was itself chosen. A whim fails because a formed character is stable. Other people are not the mind that chooses for him.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that names what character is.

feedback.note: Character is the self one builds, by choices rather than by inheritance, receipt, or a feeling. Inherits fails because the self is not issued at birth, receives fails because other people do not install it, and feels fails because a mood is not the policy the choices make. The built self is still a fact.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that says how a self is both chosen and real.

feedback.note: Character is a self built by choice and still a fact, so origin and reality are both kept. An innate stamp would deny the building, and a social product would deny that the choices were his. Further choice can change the fact. The present fact is not erased by that possibility, because a product of choice is still real.

exercises.prompt: How does a choice become part of a person's character?

choices.text: By being repeated until it is his standing policy
By being felt on one occasion, however he acts afterward
By being announced, whether or not he acts on the announcement
By having been innate, so it was a policy before any choice

feedback.note: A choice becomes character when it is repeated until it is his standing policy. One feeling or one announcement fails because a self is not formed by a single episode he does not live by. Innateness fails because the policy is the record of choices, not a code he had before he chose.

exercises.prompt: A person tells the truth once and thereafter lies whenever lying is convenient. Has honesty become his character?

choices.text: Yes. One act rewrites him into a standing virtue
No. A policy is the choice he repeats, not one act and not a wish to be described as honest
Yes. The wish to be called honest is already the policy
No. Honesty cannot be a character, because only evasions become habitual

feedback.note: Honesty has not become his character, because the choice he repeats is the lie when it is convenient. One act does not install a virtue, and a wish to be described as honest is not the policy. Vices automate in the same way virtues do. A bad repeated choice is a character too.

exercises.prompt: A course of action now runs without a fresh debate on every occasion. What has happened?

choices.text: The ease proves he never chose, because facility cancels origin
An instinct of self-preservation has taken the action over
A chosen policy has become habitual. It is still his policy, not a foreign mechanism
The capacity to choose has been repealed by the habit

feedback.note: A chosen policy has become habitual, which means it runs without a new debate each time, and it remains his policy. Ease does not cancel the choices that formed it. Instinct fails because the habit is not an innate code, and repeal fails because the capacity to focus is still there.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to what it is in the forming of character.

pairs.right: What builds a standing policy
Character, once the choice has become his usual course
Not yet a character
The policy running without a new debate each time

feedback.note: Repetition builds the policy, the policy is the character, and the habit is that policy running without a fresh debate each time. One isolated act is not yet that self. The habit is not an innate reflex and not a mechanism that chose itself, because it was made by the choices he repeated.

exercises.prompt: Does habitual here mean the action became mindless in the way a reflex is mindless?

choices.text: No. A chosen policy has become his usual course. It is not an innate reflex
Yes. Character succeeds only when it is indistinguishable from digestion
Yes. A habit is evidence that the policy was instinctive from birth
No. A habit is unreal, so there is no usual course to describe

feedback.note: Habitual names a chosen policy that has become his usual course, not a mindless reflex like digestion and not an instinct present from birth. Unreality fails because the standing policy is a fact about him. The usual course can still be reconsidered, because habit is not the repeal of choice.

exercises.prompt: A person repeatedly evades a fact he does not want. Is that evasion part of his character?

choices.text: No. Only virtues are character. A vice is always a mere lapse
No. A repeated evasion proves he never had a choice
No. Vices are stamped on by other people and have no agent
Yes. A bad policy is a self he has built. It is not a fate and not a single lapse

feedback.note: Repeated evasion is a policy, so it is character, a self he has built. Restricting character to virtues fails because a vice automates by the same kind of repetition. Fate and a social stamp fail because the evasions were choices. Naming the policy does not repeal the choice to stop repeating it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about what repeated choices become.

feedback.note: Repeated choices become one's standing policy, which is the self called character. Instinct fails because the policy was not innate, a mood fails because a feeling is not the repeated choice, and an alibi fails because the policy is a fact about him rather than an excuse that nobody chose.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that says how character is formed.

feedback.note: Character forms when choices are repeated until they are policy, which is automation in the only sense that fits a chosen self. Innate would remove the repetition, and excused would treat the policy as if it had no author. A single act is not yet that policy, because a policy is what the repetition makes.

exercises.prompt: What is prior to character, so that character cannot be the base of choice?

choices.text: Volition, the choice to focus or not. Character is a product of choices
A finished temperament, which causes the power to choose
Society, which writes both the temperament and the choices
An instinct that makes any choice to focus unnecessary

feedback.note: Volition is prior, because character is a product of choices and the primary choice is to focus or not. A finished temperament as the cause reverses that order. Society fails because other people do not choose for him, and instinct fails because he has no automatic code in place of the choice.

exercises.prompt: Why can character not be the foundation of the choice to think?

choices.text: Because character is unreal, and thinking leaves no product
Because the choices that build character include the choice to think. A product is not the source
Because thinking is automatic, so nothing is foundational
Because which fact is basic is a matter of preference

feedback.note: Character cannot found the choice to think, because that choice is among the choices that build character. A product is not the source of the capacity that produced it. Unreality fails because the product is a fact, automatic thought fails because focus is volitional, and preference fails because the order is not optional.

exercises.prompt: A theory explains thinking as the result of people simply being brave or cowardly. What has it reversed?

choices.text: Nothing. Traits are innate causes of the power to think
It has wrongly admitted that people are able to think
The order. A policy of focusing or of evading is what builds the courage or the cowardice
It has confused a personal policy with a group mind

feedback.note: The theory reverses the order. Courage and cowardice are policies built by focusing or evading, not innate causes of the power to think. Admitting thought is not the error. A group mind is a different confusion. The trait is real as a later product, and it is not the base.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its place in the dependence of character on choice.

pairs.left: The choice to focus or not
pairs.right: The primary act, prior to any policy
A later product of choices

pairs.left: Character as the cause of volition
pairs.right: The reversal to reject
Not the base of the power to think

feedback.note: The choice to focus or not is primary, and character is a later product of choices. Treating character as the cause of volition, or a finished temperament as the base, reverses the dependence. Later does not mean unreal. It means the policy rests on a choice it cannot replace as the foundation.

exercises.prompt: Does calling character later than volition mean a formed character is less than a fact?

choices.text: No. Later names dependence on choice. The product is still a real fact
Yes. Only the present moment exists, so a policy is a fiction
Yes. Whatever depends on choice is thereby nonexistent
No, because character is really the base and later is only a phrase

feedback.note: Later names dependence, not unreality. A formed character is a fact produced by choices. Reducing existence to the present moment fails because a policy endures, and dependence does not cancel a fact. Putting character at the base fails because the choice to think is what the policy rests on.

exercises.prompt: A child looks or drifts, and decades later he has a character. Which fact is the base?

choices.text: The adult character, which reaches backward and explains the child's choice
The culture, which is the base of both the child and the adult
The adult character, because it was innate and the childhood choice is a myth
The choice to focus or not. The later character is what repeated choices have made

feedback.note: The base is the choice to focus or not. The character decades later is what repeated choices have made, so it cannot explain the childhood choice by reaching backward. Culture is not the chooser, and an innate adult character fails because the policy was built across those years. The product remains real.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about how character stands to the choice to think.

parts.text: of the choice to think or not.

feedback.note: Character is a later product of the choice to think or not, so the choice is the base and the policy is the result. Cause would reverse the order, substitute would pretend the policy can stand in for the choice, and stamp would hand the product to other people. The product is a fact, and it is not the foundation, because a result cannot found the choice that produced it.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that places volition and character in order.

feedback.note: Volition is the base and character is its later product, because policies are built by the choice to think or not. Calling character the cause of volition reverses the dependence, and a social stamp denies that he is the one who chooses. The later fact is real precisely as a product.

exercises.prompt: A person has a long habit of careful thought. Which act does that habit still leave necessary?

choices.text: The present choice to focus on the facts now in front of him
Nothing. A good habit perceives those facts in his place
A fresh innate essence to approve the habit before it may operate
Permission from other people before he is allowed to look

feedback.note: The habit does not replace the present choice to focus, because a policy does not perceive today's facts for him. A habit that looks in his place would be a substitute for volition, which it is not. An innate essence and a permission slip fail because the choice is his and it is still open.

exercises.prompt: Someone says his character made him evade, so he had no choice. What is the reply?

choices.text: He is right. A habit repeals the choice to focus
The policy was built by earlier choices, and the choice to focus remains open
The evasion was an innate code asserting itself
Other people made the choice and lent him the resulting character

feedback.note: The reply is that the policy was built by earlier choices and does not close the choice to focus. A habit does not repeal volition. An innate code fails because the evasions were chosen and repeated, and other people fail as the authors because the policy is his. A formed character is a fact, not a veto.

exercises.prompt: My good character guarantees I will not evade tomorrow, so I need not watch the choice. What is the matching error?

choices.text: Good character is innate, and an innate policy cannot be lost
Watching a choice insults the policy and ought to be avoided
A good policy is not a substitute either. Tomorrow's focus is still a choice, which is why a virtue can be lost
A sincere self-description guarantees the actions that follow it

feedback.note: The flattering form is the same error: a good policy does not substitute for the choice to focus, so a virtue can be lost if he stops choosing it. Innateness fails because the policy was built. Sincerity fails because a description does not enact tomorrow's thought. The worth of the virtue is real, and it is not a guarantee.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the fact or the error it names.

pairs.right: Character already formed
Still required, and not replaced by that policy

pairs.left: It made me, so I had no choice
pairs.right: Determinism under the name of character

pairs.left: I no longer need to choose
pairs.right: The same error, stated in a flattering form

feedback.note: A standing policy is character already formed, and the present choice to focus is not replaced by it. Both the excuse that it made him and the boast that he need no longer choose treat the policy as a substitute for volition. One slanders the capacity, and the other pretends a virtue cannot be lost, because tomorrow's focus is still his choice.

exercises.prompt: A careful pilot enters a storm and stops checking the instruments, saying that is not the sort of person he is. What has he done?

choices.text: He has treated character as a substitute for focusing on these facts
He has used reason as his means of dealing with the storm
He has rightly let a good character read the instruments for him
He has changed the storm by confidence in his character

feedback.note: He has treated character as a substitute for the choice to focus on these instruments and this storm. The policy does not perceive for him. Confidence does not change the storm, because volition is not a power to rewrite facts. A good character makes care more ready, and it does not perform today's attention.

exercises.prompt: If character does not stand in for the choice to focus, is a formed virtue worthless?

choices.text: Yes. A virtue is a fiction unless it is infallible
Yes. Only the present second exists, so a policy is nothing
No. The virtue chooses in his place, which is what gives it worth
No. It is a real policy that makes the right action more ready, and it does not repeal the choice

feedback.note: A formed virtue is not worthless. It is a real policy that makes the right action more ready, and that worth does not repeal the choice to focus. Infallibility is not required for a policy to be a fact. The present second is not the whole of a self. A virtue that chose for him would be the substitute the point denies.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about the limit on a formed character.

parts.text: A formed character is not a substitute for the choice to

feedback.note: A formed character is not a substitute for the choice to focus, whether the policy is a virtue or a vice. Drift is what one may choose instead, not the act the policy replaces. Inherit and conform fail because the open choice is his exercise of attention, not a birthright and not a crowd's instruction.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that covers both a good policy and a bad one.

feedback.note: Neither a virtue nor a vice replaces the choice to focus, because a standing policy is not a substitute for volition. An excuse would use a bad policy to deny authorship, and a guarantee would use a good policy to deny that tomorrow's attention is still a choice. The policy remains a fact, and the choice remains open.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about free will and character?
exercises.quote: That which you call your soul or spirit is your consciousness, and that which you call "free will" is your mind's freedom to think or not, the only will you have, your only freedom, the choice that controls all the choices you make and determines your life and your character.

choices.text: Free will is a detachable soul's power to rewrite facts it dislikes
Free will is a guarantee that any whim will succeed without thought
Character is innate, so the choice to think does not determine it
Free will is the freedom to think or not, and that choice determines one's character

feedback.quote: That which you call your soul or spirit is your consciousness, and that which you call "free will" is your mind's freedom to think or not, the only will you have, your only freedom, the choice that controls all the choices you make and determines your life and your character.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 127
feedback.note: The passage establishes that what is called the soul is consciousness, and that free will is the mind's freedom to think or not, the choice that determines one's life and character. Rewriting facts fails because the freedom named is the freedom to think, a whim's success is not promised, and an innate character contradicts the claim that this choice determines character.

exercises.prompt: In what order do free will and character stand?

choices.text: Character first, with the freedom to think as a story told afterward
The choice to think or not first, and then the self those choices build into a policy
A detachable soul first, with neither thinking nor the body involved
Success at a whim first, with the facts arranging themselves around it

feedback.note: The choice to think or not comes first, and character is the self those choices build when they are repeated into a policy. Starting from character fails because it reverses the dependence. A detachable soul splits the person, and success at a whim pretends volition rewrites facts or guarantees an outcome. It does neither.

exercises.prompt: Someone says free will means a locked door opens because he declares it open. What is the error?

choices.text: Volition is the choice to think or not, not a power to rewrite facts
He has stated that existence is independent of his declaration
Freedom means the door has no identity of its own
A declaration is true whenever his character is sincere

feedback.note: The error treats free will as a power to rewrite facts. The only will he has is the choice to think or not, and a declaration does not open a locked door. Independence of the facts is what he denied, not what he stated. Sincerity fails because a policy of confidence is not a cause that changes the lock.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to the power it names or fails to name.

pairs.right: The only will a person has
The self that choice builds into a policy
Not what free will is
Not a promise that comes with volition

feedback.note: The only will is the freedom to think or not, and character is the self that choice builds into a policy. Rewriting the facts and success at any whim are not included. A formed character, good or bad, remains a fact that further choice can change. It does not become a license over reality.

exercises.prompt: A wish to be a great inventor, pursued with no study, is called free will in action. What is confused?

choices.text: The craft with an innate code, so study would be a confession that he is determined
The wish with a value-judgment that has already discovered the craft
The freedom to think with a guarantee that any whim will succeed. The work still has requirements
Ambition with a power that creates the facts of the craft by wanting them

feedback.note: Free will is the freedom to think, not a guarantee that a whim will succeed. The craft has requirements, and study is thinking and acting on them. An innate code fails because invention is not given, the wish is not yet knowledge of the craft, and wanting does not create the facts the work has to respect.

exercises.prompt: A formed habit of evasion is a fact, and the person can still choose to focus. Which of those clauses can be dropped?

choices.text: Neither. Drop the habit's reality and character is a fiction. Drop the open choice and the habit is a prison
The habit's reality, because only the present choice exists
The open choice, because a formed policy repeals volition
Both, because other people decide whether he evaded and whether he can think

feedback.note: Neither clause can be dropped. The habit is a fact because repeated choices made it, and the choice to focus remains because a policy is not a substitute for volition. Keeping only the present moment makes character a fiction. Keeping only the policy makes it a prison. Other people are not the chooser.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about what free will does not rewrite.

parts.text: Free will does not rewrite the

feedback.note: Free will does not rewrite the facts, because the only freedom it names is the choice to think or not. Effort, mind, and policy fail as the thing it cannot touch, because effort and attention are exactly what that choice initiates, and a policy is the character the choice builds. The world's identity remains what it is.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that joins the choice to think with the self one builds.

feedback.note: The choice to think or not determines the character one builds, once those choices are repeated into a policy. Rewrites the facts would turn volition into a decree over reality, and guarantees a whim would promise success the world's nature does not owe him. The policy he has built is a fact, and further choice can change it.

exercises.prompt: What is an emotion, in relation to a person's values?

choices.text: An automatic result of a value-judgment he holds
A tool that discovers facts the judgment has not reached
An innate code of knowledge about what is good for him
A command issued by a group in place of his judgment

feedback.note: An emotion is an automatic result of a value-judgment, not a first report of the world. Calling it a tool of discovery fails because the judgment is already the estimate, an innate code fails because the content of his values is not given, and a group's command fails because the estimate is his.

exercises.prompt: Two people see the same promotion. One is glad and the other is resentful. Where does the difference lie?

choices.text: In the facts of the promotion, which differ for each viewer
In their value-judgments about the promotion, not in the event
In their eyes, which manufacture two different events
In a group mind that assigns feelings and skips judgment

feedback.note: The event is the same, so the different emotions follow from different value-judgments about it. Moving the difference into the facts fails because the promotion did not become two events, and the eyes did not invent it. A group mind fails because each person estimates according to his own values.

exercises.prompt: Can a person produce an emotion by a sheer decision to feel it, with no evaluation underneath?

choices.text: Yes. Emotions are chosen directly, and judgments are optional decorations
Yes. A decision to feel is a tool that discovers a new fact
No. An emotion follows from an evaluation. It is not painted on by will
No. Emotions are uncaused, so evaluations never give rise to them

feedback.note: An emotion is an automatic consequence of an evaluation, so a sheer decision to feel, with no judgment under it, does not produce one. Direct choice fails because the will does not manufacture feelings. Calling emotions uncaused fails because the value-judgment is precisely their cause.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its role in an emotional response.

pairs.right: An automatic result of a value-judgment
The estimate that gives rise to the feeling
Evidence of two different evaluations
Not a cause that produces an emotion

feedback.note: The value-judgment is the estimate, and the emotion is its automatic result, which is why one event can yield two feelings. A sheer decision to feel is not the cause. Treating the feeling as the discoverer of the event reverses the dependence, because the estimate was already there.

exercises.prompt: Someone says your emotions prove you were born with your values already set. What is confused?

choices.text: The innate capacity to feel is confused with an innate content of values
Emotions are confused with sensations, as if a feeling were a sensory given
The good is confused with a property that objects reveal without judgment
Nothing. Emotions are an automatic code of true value-judgments

feedback.note: The capacity to feel is part of his nature, and the content of his value-judgments is not innate. Emotions follow the judgments he has formed, so they are not proof of a code he was born holding. An infallible code fails because a judgment behind an emotion can be false.

exercises.prompt: An emotion can be appropriate. Why does that not make the emotion the primary fact?

choices.text: An appropriate emotion bypasses judgment and perceives the fact directly
Appropriateness means the feeling made the fact true
An appropriate emotion is one he willed into existence for the occasion
It is appropriate when the value-judgment is true. The truth lies in that judgment

feedback.note: An appropriate emotion follows a true value-judgment, so the truth is in the judgment's relation to the facts, and the feeling remains a consequence. Bypass fails because the emotion does not perceive on its own, and willing the feeling fails because emotions are not painted on. The feeling does not make the fact true.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that says what emotions result from.

feedback.note: Emotions are automatic results of value-judgments, including judgments held without being put into a sentence. Bare sensations fail because a percept is not an evaluation, innate codes fail because the content is not given at birth, and group orders fail because the estimate is the person's own.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that states what an emotion is.

feedback.note: An emotion is an automatic result of a value-judgment, so it reports the estimate rather than discovering the fact. A tool of cognition would give it the office of reason, and an innate code would pretend the values were written in. Neither produces the feeling, because the feeling follows an estimate the person has formed.

exercises.prompt: A feeling is intense. What does the intensity settle about the facts?

choices.text: Nothing. Intensity shows how strong the estimate is, not whether it is true
That the estimate is true, because strength is a standard of truth
That the facts have rearranged themselves to match the feeling
That no estimate is involved, because a strong feeling is a pure given

feedback.note: Intensity shows the strength of the estimate, and it settles nothing about the facts, because a powerful error is still an error. Strength as a standard of truth fails because force is not evidence. A pure given fails because the feeling is already an evaluation, not a percept with no judgment in it.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about what a feeling reports?
exercises.quote: What you feel tells you nothing about the facts; it merely tells you something about your estimate of the facts.

choices.text: A feeling reports your estimate of the facts and does not report the facts
A feeling reports the facts and reports nothing about the person who feels it
A feeling reports nothing of either kind, so it is only noise to be discarded
A feeling changes the facts until they match the estimate

feedback.quote: What you feel tells you nothing about the facts; it merely tells you something about your estimate of the facts.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, interview with Alvin Toffler, Playboy, March 1964
feedback.note: The passage establishes that a feeling tells you nothing about the facts and does tell you something about your estimate of them. Reporting the facts reverses the point. Discarding the feeling as noise drops the estimate it reveals, and changing the facts to match the estimate treats a state of the person as a cause of reality.

exercises.prompt: You dread a medical result and feel sure it will be bad. What does the dread report?

choices.text: The laboratory facts, ahead of any test
Your estimate that the outcome will be bad, not the outcome itself
The physician's knowledge, transferred into the feeling
A perception of the result that did not need the evidence

feedback.note: The dread reports your estimate of the outcome, not the outcome. The laboratory facts are not in the feeling, and the physician's knowledge is not transferred by dread. A perception that skips the evidence fails because fear is not a sense organ. The estimate can be checked, and the feeling cannot replace the check.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to what it reports, and to what it does not report.

pairs.right: Your estimate of the facts
Not what the feeling establishes
How strong the estimate is, not whether it is true
Still an estimate, and still not the facts

feedback.note: A feeling reports your estimate, calm or intense, true or false as a judgment, and it does not establish the facts. Intensity fails as a measure of truth because strength is not evidence. A calm error is still only an estimate, so quietness does not make a false judgment into a fact.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, I feel confident, so the plan is sound. Which error is that?

choices.text: The error of consulting the relevant facts before acting
The error of forming any estimate at all
Subjectivism. Confidence is an estimate. The plan is sound only if the facts support it
No error, if confidence helps him start, because a useful feeling is a true one

feedback.note: Confidence reports his estimate of the plan, not the plan's soundness, so treating the feeling as proof is subjectivism. Usefulness fails as a rescue because a feeling that helps him start can still be an estimate of a plan the facts will not support. Consulting the facts is the check, not the error.

exercises.prompt: A feeling can be a clue to your own premises. What does that clue not become?

choices.text: Evidence of the external facts. It points to your estimate, which still has to be checked
Anything at all, so every emotion should be discarded as noise
A consequence of a value-judgment, because a clue has no cause
A state of a living person, because only facts without knowers are real

feedback.note: The clue tells you something about your estimate, and it does not become evidence of the facts, because the estimate can be wrong. Discarding every emotion fails because the clue to your own judgment is real. A causeless clue fails because the value-judgment is the cause. The person who feels is real.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about what a feeling reports.

parts.text: of the facts, not the facts themselves.

feedback.note: A feeling reports your estimate of the facts, not the facts themselves. Proof fails because the estimate still has to be checked against the evidence, creation fails because the feeling does not make the facts, and erasure fails because refusing to feel does not remove either the facts or the judgment.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that limits what a feeling can tell you.

feedback.note: A feeling reports your estimate rather than the facts themselves, so it is a clue to the judgment and not a piece of evidence about the world. Creates would make the feeling the author of the facts, and replaces would let the estimate stand in for the check, because the estimate can still be false.

exercises.prompt: What does a tool of cognition do, in the role that emotions are denied?

choices.text: It identifies facts and integrates them into knowledge
It registers an evaluation one already holds
It punishes the body for having any desires
It takes a vote on what shall count as true

feedback.note: A tool of cognition identifies facts and integrates them into knowledge, which is reason's office. An emotion registers an evaluation already held, so it is not doing that work. Punishment and voting fail because neither is identification. Denying the office to emotion does not deny the emotion's cause.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about emotions and knowledge?
exercises.quote: Emotions are not tools of cognition.

choices.text: Emotions are the primary means by which a person identifies facts
Emotions are not means of identifying and integrating facts
Emotions have no causes, because they are not tools of cognition
Reason is in the same position, so nothing is a means of knowledge

feedback.quote: Emotions are not tools of cognition.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, interview with Alvin Toffler, Playboy, March 1964
feedback.note: The passage establishes that emotions are not tools of cognition, so they do not identify facts. Making them the primary means reverses the sentence. Causelessness does not follow, because an emotion is still the result of a value-judgment. Skepticism about reason does not follow either, because the denial is aimed at emotions, not at every faculty.

exercises.prompt: Someone says he will decide whether a witness lied by noticing how angry he feels. What is he treating as a cognitive tool?

choices.text: The testimony, which he thinks should be ignored whenever a feeling is present
His anger, which cannot identify whether the witness lied
Reason, which he thinks anger improves by replacing evidence
A value-judgment, which he thinks has no connection with anger

feedback.note: He is treating anger as a tool of cognition, and anger cannot identify whether the witness lied. The feeling follows his estimate of the witness, which is exactly why it is not independent evidence. Anger does not improve reason by replacing the testimony. The value-judgment is the anger's cause, not a stranger to it.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the cognitive job it has or does not have.

pairs.right: Identifies and integrates the facts
Not a tool of cognition
The estimate of which the emotion is a result
Established by evidence, not by the feeling

feedback.note: Reason identifies and integrates, a fact is established by evidence, and an emotion is the result of a value-judgment rather than a tool that discovers the fact. Giving the emotion reason's job fails because the feeling tells you about the estimate. The estimate itself still has to be checked by reason.

exercises.prompt: A mystic says a special feeling is a higher way of knowing than reason. What is the error?

choices.text: The error is having any values, because evaluation causes feeling
A feeling that contradicts the facts can still count as knowledge if it is special
A feeling is not a means of knowledge, higher or ordinary. It follows an evaluation
Mysticism is reason used quickly, so the feeling is a rapid faculty

feedback.note: A special feeling is not a higher means of knowledge, because no feeling identifies facts. It remains a consequence of an evaluation. Letting it contradict the facts and still count as knowledge abandons identification. Speed fails because a quick feeling is not reason. Having values is not the error.

exercises.prompt: Emotions are not tools of cognition, so, someone infers, they have no causes and no tie to ideas. What has he dropped?

choices.text: They result from value-judgments. Denying that they discover facts does not make them causeless
He has dropped nothing, because a cause would turn them into innate knowledge
He should restore them as tools of cognition
Ideas are feelings, so the dependence runs from the feeling to the fact

feedback.note: He has dropped the cause. Emotions are results of value-judgments even though they are not tools of cognition. A cause does not make them innate knowledge, because the judgment can be learned and can be false. Restoring them as tools reverses the correction, and ideas are not feelings.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that states the cognitive limit on a feeling.

parts.text: A feeling is not a means of

feedback.note: A feeling is not a means of knowledge, because it does not identify and integrate facts. Metabolism, exchange, and motion fail in that place because the denied office is cognition, not life, trade, or physical movement. The feeling remains a real result of a value-judgment, which is why the limit is not a claim that emotions have no cause.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that keeps a feeling from being used as proof.

feedback.note: A feeling does not discover the facts it reacts to, because those facts are identified by reason and the feeling follows an estimate of them. Create would make the feeling the author of the facts, and replace would let it stand in for the judgment. Neither is compatible with the denial that emotions are tools of cognition.

exercises.prompt: What is the order between a value-judgment and the emotion that expresses it?

choices.text: The value-judgment comes first, and the emotion follows automatically
The emotion comes first and writes the judgment afterward
The facts reshape themselves to fit the feeling, and judgment copies that
A group assigns the feeling, and no judgment occurs in the person

feedback.note: The value-judgment comes first, and the emotion follows as its automatic result. Reversing the order fails because the feeling does not invent the estimate it expresses. Facts do not reshape themselves to fit a feeling, and a group does not assign the emotion in place of the person's own judgment.

exercises.prompt: You conclude that a colleague cheated you, and then you feel contempt. What came first in you?

choices.text: The contempt, which then created the judgment that he cheated
The judgment that he cheated you. The contempt is its emotional result
The contempt, which by itself established the cheating as a fact
A causeless reflex, of which the conclusion is a story that does not count

feedback.note: The judgment came first, and the contempt is its result. Letting the contempt create the judgment reverses the order, and letting it establish the cheating treats an emotion as proof. A causeless reflex fails because the estimate that he cheated is the cause of the feeling.

exercises.prompt: Can you summon love or fear as a method of learning a fact you have not yet judged?

choices.text: Yes, because a feeling is a tool of cognition
Yes, because the first feeling defines what the fact is
No. An emotion follows an evaluation. It is not a probe sent out to collect facts
No, because emotions have no relation to any evaluation

feedback.note: You cannot summon love or fear as a probe, because an emotion follows an evaluation and does not go out to collect a fact. Treating it as a tool of cognition reverses the order. Denying any relation to evaluation fails in the other direction, because the judgment is what the feeling expresses.

exercises.prompt: Match each step or story to its place in the order.

pairs.right: Comes before the emotion
Follows from that judgment
The order reversed

pairs.left: A decision to feel at once
pairs.right: An attempt to skip the judgment

feedback.note: Judgment comes before the emotion, and the emotion follows, because the feeling is a result rather than a probe. The story that the feeling writes the judgment reverses that order. A decision to feel at once tries to skip the estimate. Implicit premises are still judgments, not an exception in which the feeling leads.

exercises.prompt: You accept that he did not cheat you. What can change the contempt?

choices.text: The new judgment, because the emotion results from the estimate, and the estimate has changed
Nothing. The original contempt remains proof that he cheated
A decision to feel nothing, while the old estimate is carefully kept
A vote that the feeling, not the new evidence, settles what happened

feedback.note: The new judgment can change the contempt because the emotion depends on the estimate. Keeping the old estimate and ordering the feeling to vanish fails because the cause is still in place. Treating the original contempt as proof ignores the evidence. A vote cannot replace the revised judgment.

exercises.prompt: You do not always recite a sentence before a feeling. What is still true of the order?

choices.text: A feeling with no evaluation is the ordinary case, and it discovers the facts
Implicit means innate, so the emotion is an infallible code
What is stored was caused by the emotion, which came first
An evaluation may be stored without a recited sentence. It is still first, and the emotion follows

feedback.note: A stored evaluation is still a judgment, so the emotion still follows it even when no sentence was recited. The ordinary case is not a feeling with no evaluation. Implicit does not mean innate or infallible, because a stored premise can be false. The feeling did not cause the premise it expresses.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about the order of judgment and emotion.

feedback.note: The value-judgment comes before the emotion, as its cause. After reverses the order, without denies the cause, and instead of pretends the judgment replaces the feeling rather than giving rise to it. You change a mistaken emotion by reconsidering the judgment, not by commanding the feeling while the judgment stays.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that keeps judgment and emotion in order.

feedback.note: The judgment comes first and the emotion follows, including when the judgment is a stored premise rather than a speech. Invents the facts would make the feeling a tool of cognition, and replaces reason would drop the faculty that checks the judgment. Both fail because they reverse the order the feeling actually has.

exercises.prompt: A measurement says a structure is unsafe, and you feel sure it is fine. What do you re-check?

choices.text: The estimate behind the calm, against the measurement. You do not edit the measurement
The measurement, until it agrees with the feeling
Nothing. A calm feeling outranks an instrument
Your duty to feel whatever the people around you feel

feedback.note: You re-check the estimate behind the calm, because a feeling reports that estimate and not the safety of the structure. Editing the measurement to fit the feeling treats an emotion as evidence. Calm does not outrank an instrument, and the group's mood is not a second measurement.

exercises.prompt: The structure is unsafe, your judgment agrees, and you feel fear. What is that fear?

choices.text: A tool of cognition that can replace the inspection
An appropriate emotion, because the judgment is true. The fear is still not the evidence
A defect to be erased, because fear is never an appropriate result
Proof that an emotion should be obeyed whenever it is strong

feedback.note: The fear is appropriate because the value-judgment is true, and it is still not the evidence that established the danger. Replacing the inspection fails because the emotion did not discover the fact. Erasing every fear fails because an appropriate result is not a defect, and strength is not a reason to obey it.

exercises.prompt: When is an emotion mistaken rather than appropriate?

choices.text: Whenever it occurs, because feeling as such is an error
Only when it is unpleasant. A pleasant emotion is knowledge
When the value-judgment it expresses is false, however powerful the feeling
When it differs from the mood of the surrounding group

feedback.note: An emotion is mistaken when the value-judgment it expresses is false. Power does not repair a false estimate. Calling every feeling an error fails because a true judgment has an appropriate emotional result, and pleasure fails as a test because a pleasant estimate can be false. The group's mood is not the standard.

exercises.prompt: Match each result or policy to what it does with a feeling.

pairs.right: Follows a true value-judgment
Follows a false value-judgment
Treats an estimate as if it were the fact
Treats a real consequence as an enemy

feedback.note: Appropriateness tracks a true judgment, and a mistake tracks a false one. Obeying the feeling treats the estimate as the fact, which emotions cannot establish. Blanking every feeling treats a real consequence as an enemy. Neither policy checks the judgment, which is the step the clash requires.

exercises.prompt: One rule says never feel fear. Another says always act on fear. What do both rules drop?

choices.text: The judgment. One tries to erase a consequence, and the other treats the consequence as knowledge
Nothing. Each rule is right during a different hour
Fear's cause, because fear is an innate code with no judgment behind it
The facts, which should be rewritten until one of the rules feels comfortable

feedback.note: Both rules drop the judgment. Erasing fear treats a consequence as an enemy, and always acting on it treats the consequence as knowledge. Fear is not an innate code. Rewriting the facts to suit a rule is the primacy of consciousness. The alternative is to check the estimate against the facts.

exercises.prompt: You accept evidence of a fraud, and admiration for the person lingers. Which description fits?

choices.text: The lag proves the fraud is unreal, because a good feeling outlasts evidence
The lag proves that emotions discover facts after the evidence is in
You should announce that the feeling is gone while the old estimate stays in place
The old estimate is still at work, so the feeling has lagged. Re-check that estimate, and do not treat the lag as proof

feedback.note: The lingering admiration means the old estimate is still operating, so the emotion has not yet followed the new judgment. Treating the lag as proof of innocence uses a feeling as evidence. Announcing the feeling gone while the estimate stays commands a consequence and leaves its cause. The thing to re-check is the judgment.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about a clash between a feeling and a fact.

parts.text: , and do not treat the feeling as evidence.

feedback.note: Re-check the judgment, because the feeling is only its emotional result and may be appropriate or mistaken with it. Intensity fails because strength is not evidence, the crowd fails because its mood is not your measurement, and appetite fails because a desire is not a re-examination of the estimate.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle for a clash between feeling and fact.

feedback.note: Check the judgment rather than obeying the feeling or blanking it, because the emotion can be appropriate or mistaken only through the truth or falsehood of the estimate. Rewriting the fact hands the world to the feeling, and polling the crowd substitutes another unexamined estimate. Neither looks at the judgment.

exercises.prompt: Which picture sets a human mind and a human body against each other as enemies?

choices.text: A ghostly mind at war with a mechanical body
One organism, with awareness as a faculty of that living body
Reason as an attribute of the individual person
Consciousness as awareness of what exists

feedback.note: The false picture is a ghostly mind at war with a mechanical body, two enemies sharing one life. The alternatives fail as descriptions of that war because they state the fact the war denies: one organism, whose awareness is a faculty and whose reason is his own attribute.

exercises.prompt: The advice to punish the body so a soul can be free assumes which picture?

choices.text: Man is one organism, so damaging the body damages the person
Mind and body are enemies, and the body is the lower one to be defeated
Consciousness is the faculty of awareness of a living organism
Reason belongs to the individual, not to a detachable spirit

feedback.note: Punishing the body to free a soul assumes the war: a higher ghost and a lower machine. One organism fails as a reading of that advice because an integrated person is harmed, not freed, when his body is treated as an enemy. The advice does not describe a faculty of awareness.

exercises.prompt: The claim that awareness is a chemical fiction, and that nothing is really conscious, keeps which half of the split?

choices.text: The ghostly half, on which a soul thinks with no body at all
Neither half, because denying a ghost already affirms one organism
The mechanical half, on which the body is mindless and awareness is not real
Both halves reconciled, because chemistry is a form of revelation

feedback.note: Denying that anyone is aware keeps the mechanical half of the split: a mindless body, with consciousness dismissed as fiction. It does not affirm one organism, because an organism of man's kind is conscious. Revelation fails because a chemical description is not a message from a spirit.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the false picture to what it caricatures.

pairs.right: Awareness treated as a spirit apart from the person
The organism treated as a mindless device
The claim that the two are enemies
The fact that picture denies

feedback.note: The war caricatures awareness as a separate spirit and the organism as a mindless device, then sets them against each other. One living organism is the fact that picture denies, because consciousness is a faculty of that organism rather than a rival tenant. Neither caricature is a description of man's nature.

exercises.prompt: Why is that war not a fact of human nature?

choices.text: Man is one entity of a specific nature, and awareness is a faculty of that organism
Minds do not exist, so only mindless machines are real
Bodies are illusions projected by a soul
A vote can declare the two enemies reconciled

feedback.note: The war is not a fact of human nature because man is one entity of a specific nature, and his consciousness is the awareness of that living organism. Denying the mind fails because awareness is real, denying the body fails because the organism is real, and a vote fails because nature is not settled by agreement.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the mind is a driver and the body is a car. Why is this still the same error?

choices.text: It correctly treats man as one organism with a faculty of awareness
It is harmless, because a comparison cannot state a real split
It is true, because tools and living organisms are the same kind of entity
It makes consciousness a separate agent and the body a vehicle the agent uses

feedback.note: The driver and the car are the ghost and the machine in a calmer tone, because the mind is cast as a separate agent and the body as a vehicle. Calling the comparison harmless fails because this comparison is the split. Tools and organisms are not the same kind of entity, since only the organism is conscious.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejection of the split between mind and body.

parts.text: Mind and body are not two

feedback.note: Mind and body are not two enemies, because they are aspects of one organism of a specific nature. Wishes, ballots, and moods fail as the thing they are not, because the error is the war between a ghostly mind and a mechanical body, not a disagreement of tastes.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that names the two caricatures and drops the war.

feedback.note: A ghostly mind is not at war with a mechanical body, because man is one organism and neither caricature is a fact of his nature. A chosen ally would turn the split into a friendship of two beings, and a mere fiction would deny awareness along with the ghost. The rejection drops both enemies rather than crowning one of them.

exercises.prompt: What is the relation of consciousness to the living human body?

choices.text: It is the faculty of awareness of that one organism, not a second tenant
It is a ghost that can depart and remain a mind without the organism
It is a byproduct that only seems to be awareness
It is an attribute of the crowd, stored for a while in one body

feedback.note: Consciousness is the faculty of awareness of one living organism, so the person is not a body plus a tenant. A departing ghost fails because awareness is an attribute of the organism, a mere seeming fails because the awareness is real, and a crowd fails because the faculty belongs to the individual.

exercises.prompt: A physician treats an injury, and the injured person judges the evidence about his care. What follows about mind and body?

choices.text: The physician owns a machine, and the patient is only a ghost in it
One organism is both the living body and the being who is aware
Awareness is irrelevant to the body that was injured
The injury is a moral fault of a soul for having a body

feedback.note: One organism is injured and is the being who judges, because mind and body are aspects of that individual. A ghost in a machine fails because the patient is not a tenant of his own flesh, and irrelevance fails because the injury is his. The injury is a physical fact, not a sin of embodiment.

exercises.prompt: Match each term to the place it has in one human being.

pairs.right: The faculty of awareness of the living organism
That organism, not a device beside a mind
One entity of a specific nature
The split that integration rejects

feedback.note: Integration means one entity of a specific nature, with consciousness as its faculty of awareness and the body as that organism rather than a device. A second tenant fails because it is the split this rejects. Distinct faculties do not become two creatures, and they do not melt into a featureless lump, because a difference of attributes is not a difference of entities.

exercises.prompt: A theory says only the body exists and that reports of awareness can be dropped. What does it deny?

choices.text: That the organism has a body and acts according to its nature
That physical processes can be studied
That the organism is really aware. The body is real, and so is the faculty
That a ghost is required before any chemical process can occur

feedback.note: The theory denies real awareness while keeping the body, which is the mechanical half of the split. The body and its study are not what it denies. A ghost is not required for chemistry, and dropping the ghost does not license one to say that nobody is conscious.

exercises.prompt: Does one individual mean that awareness and a bone are the same feature, with no difference of kind?

choices.text: No. Distinct attributes of one entity are not two enemies and not one featureless lump
Yes. Otherwise mind and body would have to be two creatures
Yes. A bone thinks in concepts, and awareness is simply bone
No. They remain two creatures who merely share a name

feedback.note: One entity can have distinct attributes. Awareness is not the same feature as a bone, and the distinction does not make two creatures at war. Collapsing them into one featureless lump fails because a faculty is real, and splitting them into two beings fails because there is one organism.

exercises.prompt: If mind and body are one, may a person ignore a physical injury by attending only to ideas?

choices.text: Yes. Ideas are the person, and the injury belongs to a foreign machine
Yes. Integration means the body has no causal nature
No. Integration means ideas are impossible and only tissue is real
No. The injury is his, because the body is not a vehicle he can set aside

feedback.note: Integration means the injured body is the person, not a vehicle a mind may abandon. Setting it aside restores the ghost's contempt for the organism. Denying ideas fails in the other direction, because awareness is real. The body's causal nature remains in force.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that mind and body are aspects of one being.

feedback.note: Man is one organism of a specific nature, so consciousness and the body are attributes of that being. A ghost, a crowd, or a machine fails because each replaces the individual organism with a tenant, a collective, or a mindless device. Distinct faculties do not divide him into two entities.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that places consciousness in one living organism.

feedback.note: Consciousness is the awareness of one living organism, which is why mind and body are not two beings. A second tenant would bring the ghost back, and an illusion would deny the faculty, because awareness is real and it belongs to the organism. The organism has a specific nature, and awareness is one of its attributes.

exercises.prompt: Whose attribute is the faculty of reason?

choices.text: The individual human being's
A group mind over and above its members
A spirit world that visits people and thinks for them
Chemistry that reaches conclusions while no one is aware

feedback.note: Reason is an attribute of the individual, because only a particular consciousness identifies and integrates. A group mind fails because a group does not think, a spirit world fails because the faculty is not a visitor, and unaware chemistry fails because a conclusion with no awareness is not reason.

exercises.prompt: A committee announces a conclusion that no member has judged. What is missing?

choices.text: Nothing. A group mind knows what the members have not judged
Reason. Only an individual consciousness can identify and integrate
An instinct that makes the announcement true without judgment
A revelation that removes the need for anyone to think

feedback.note: What is missing is reason, because identifying and integrating are acts of an individual consciousness, and no member performed them. A group mind fails because there is no such thinker. Instinct and revelation fail because neither is a substitute for the judgment nobody made.

exercises.prompt: Can reason exist as a pure spirit when no living person is exercising it?

choices.text: Yes. Bodies only obstruct a mind that thinks better without them
Yes. Concepts are real only when nobody holds them
No. Reason is an attribute of a living individual, not a resident of another world
No. Reason is a reflex, and awareness of a conclusion is a fiction

feedback.note: Reason is an attribute of the living individual who exercises it, so it does not sit in a spirit world waiting to visit. A mind freed of the body is the ghost again. A reflex with no awareness fails in the other direction, because reason is a conscious faculty, not a motion that nobody identifies.

exercises.prompt: Match each alleged bearer of reason to the verdict it deserves.

pairs.right: The being whose attribute reason is
A fiction that cannot think
Not a place where the faculty resides
Not reason, because nothing has been identified

feedback.note: Reason's bearer is the individual. A group mind cannot think, a spirit world is not the faculty's home, and a reflex that no one is aware of has not identified anything. Sharing a conclusion still leaves each learner to judge it. The attribute does not migrate into the collective.

exercises.prompt: People learn from one another. Why does that not move reason into the culture as a mind?

choices.text: Each learner still has to think. Sharing a conclusion does not create a super-mind
Learning from others is impossible, because reason cannot use another person's work
A culture perceives the world and then lends sensations to its members
Each person is born already knowing the culture's conclusions

feedback.note: Shared knowledge does not move the faculty into the culture, because each person still has to identify and integrate for himself. Banning learning fails because another person's evidence can be judged. A perceiving culture fails because only individuals are conscious, and innate cultural conclusions fail because there is no such code.

exercises.prompt: If reason is an attribute of the individual, who succeeds or fails when a judgment is made?

choices.text: The collective, praised or blamed as the mind that judged
Nobody, because truth is whatever the group happens to feel
The body, conceived as a machine that thinks while the person does not
The person who judges. He cannot hand the act of thinking to a collective

feedback.note: The person who judges is the one who knows or fails to know, because the act of thinking is his. A collective cannot be the mind that judged. Feeling as the standard fails because agreement is not identification, and a machine that thinks while he does not is the mindless body again.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle about who has the faculty of reason.

parts.text: Reason is an attribute of the

feedback.note: Reason is an attribute of the individual, not of a crowd, a spirit, or a reflex. A crowd fails because it has no consciousness of its own, a spirit fails because the faculty is not a detachable tenant, and a reflex fails because reason is conscious identification rather than a motion with no awareness.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that places reason in the individual.

feedback.note: Reason is an attribute of the individual rather than of a group, because only a person identifies and integrates. A spirit would detach the faculty from the living being, and a reflex would deny that anyone is aware of the conclusion. Learning from others does not change the bearer.

exercises.prompt: What is consciousness, once a detachable soul has been dropped?

choices.text: The faculty by which a living organism is aware of what exists
A disembodied spirit that occupies a body and may leave it
An illusion, so the report of being aware is a fiction
A public mind in which individual people are temporary moods

feedback.note: Consciousness is the faculty by which a living organism is aware of what exists. Dropping a detachable soul does not drop that faculty. A spirit that leaves fails because awareness is not a tenant, an illusion fails because the awareness is real, and a public mind fails because the faculty is the individual's.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about consciousness?
exercises.quote: Consciousness is the faculty of awareness—the faculty of perceiving that which exists.

choices.text: Consciousness is a ghost that can be aware of nothing and still be a mind
Consciousness is an illusion, so the faculty of awareness is a fiction
Consciousness is the faculty of awareness, the faculty of perceiving what exists
Consciousness is a public mood rather than a faculty that perceives

feedback.quote: Consciousness is the faculty of awareness—the faculty of perceiving that which exists.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Concepts of Consciousness," Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, 37
feedback.note: The passage establishes that consciousness is the faculty of awareness, perceiving what exists, so it is an attribute of a knower rather than a tenant or a fiction. A ghost aware of nothing fails because awareness is of something, an illusion fails because the faculty is real, and a public mood fails because perceiving is not a collective feeling.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the soul leaves the body and keeps thinking without it. What kind of claim is that?

choices.text: An account of consciousness as the organism's faculty of awareness
A ghost story, in which a mind exists and knows apart from the living organism
A reminder that awareness is always awareness of something that exists
A statement that the person is one entity of a specific nature

feedback.note: A soul that thinks after leaving the body is a ghostly mind, not a faculty of the organism. Awareness of what exists cannot be parked outside the living being that perceives. The claim does not preserve one entity, because it adds a second one that is supposed to survive the organism's absence.

exercises.prompt: Match each description to the claim it makes about the mind.

pairs.right: What consciousness is
A mind alleged to exist apart from the organism
The object a faculty of awareness perceives
A ghostly tenant, not the person

feedback.note: Consciousness is a faculty of awareness, and what exists is what that faculty perceives. A disembodied soul and an occupant of the body are two names for the tenant the facts do not contain. Dropping the tenant leaves the organism's awareness. It does not leave a mind with nothing to be aware of.

exercises.prompt: Someone says that if there is no ghost, there is no consciousness. What has he assumed?

choices.text: That consciousness could only have been a ghost. The organism's faculty remains
That a faculty of awareness would be a second organism inside the first
That chemistry is false whenever a person perceives
That reason belongs to a crowd if it belongs to any person

feedback.note: He has assumed that the only possible consciousness was a ghost, so rejecting the ghost seems to reject awareness. The faculty remains because it is the living organism's awareness of what exists. Chemistry is not made false by perception, and the faculty does not become a second organism or a crowd.

exercises.prompt: A mystic says the mind knows best when it turns away from the body and the senses. What is the error?

choices.text: The senses are unreliable, so deserting them is how reason begins
The body should be conquered before any knowledge is possible
Revelation is reason under another name, so the turn is a method of identification
Knowledge is not a reward for deserting the organism. Awareness perceives what exists

feedback.note: The error is the ghost's reward for deserting the organism. Awareness is the living person's faculty of perceiving what exists, so turning away from the senses drops the material reason integrates. Conquering the body fails because it is the same war, and revelation fails because it is not identification under another name.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejection of a mind that could leave the living person.

parts.text: The mind is not a detachable

feedback.note: The mind is not a detachable soul, because consciousness is the living organism's faculty of awareness, not a tenant that could depart and keep thinking. A reflex fails because awareness is real, a ballot fails because a vote does not decide what the mind is, and a mood fails because a feeling is not the faculty that perceives what exists.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that keeps consciousness in the living organism.

feedback.note: Consciousness is a living organism's faculty of awareness, so it is not a ghost that could leave and not an illusion to be explained away. Either substitute fails because it restores one half of the split. The faculty perceives what exists, which a tenant with no organism cannot do.

exercises.prompt: What is wrong with calling the body a mindless machine the mind must conquer?

choices.text: The body is the living organism that is aware, not a device at war with a mind
Nothing. Flesh cannot be part of a being that knows
The body is an illusion, and only a ghost is real
Machines and organisms differ only by a vote about words

feedback.note: The body is the living organism that is aware, so it is not a mindless device a mind must conquer. Barring flesh from knowledge fails because the knower is that organism. An illusionary body is the ghost's half of the split, and a vote fails because the difference is a fact of nature.

exercises.prompt: A theory says awareness is only chemistry and that the report of being aware is a fiction. What does it deny?

choices.text: That organisms have bodies governed by their nature
The fact of awareness. The chemistry is real, and so is the faculty
That one may study the living body
That a ghost must approve a chemical process before it occurs

feedback.note: The theory denies awareness, which is a fact, while the chemistry of the organism remains real. Studying the body is not what it denies. A ghost's approval is not part of causality. An account that ends by saying nobody is aware has denied the faculty it set out to understand.

exercises.prompt: Does rejecting the picture of a mindless machine exempt the body from causality?

choices.text: Yes. A body that is not a machine obeys wishes rather than its nature
Yes. Disease is then a moral choice with no physical cause
No. The organism acts by its nature. What is rejected is the mindless device to be conquered
No, because the body is a ghost and ghosts cause health

feedback.note: Rejecting the machine does not exempt the body from causality, because the organism still acts according to its nature. Wishes do not replace that nature, and disease does not become a pure moral choice. The rejected claim is that the body is mindless and must be conquered, not that it has an identity.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the conclusion it supports about man.

pairs.right: Mind and body are aspects of one life
Consciousness is the organism's faculty of awareness
The body is not a device that awareness must conquer
The individual, not a group and not a spirit

feedback.note: Taken together, the claims say that man is one organism: awareness is his faculty, the body is not a device to conquer, and reason is his attribute. A ghost or a group as the bearer would undo the integration, because neither is the individual who perceives. The machine picture and the ghost picture are the two halves of one false war.

exercises.prompt: Someone says he will live as if he had no body, because the body is a trap. Which error is this?

choices.text: The ghost's contempt for the organism. The body is not a trap set by an enemy
A plain statement that man is one integrated organism
The claim that man's needs include the use of reason
The claim that reason is an attribute of the individual

feedback.note: Calling the body a trap is the ghost's contempt for the organism, which is the war in moral language. Integration fails as a reading of that sentence because the sentence denies the body rather than keeping it. Needs and the bearer of reason are different points, and neither says the body is an enemy.

exercises.prompt: A description of the brain is true, and the author adds that therefore nobody is aware and the person is a machine to be managed. What should be kept?

choices.text: The denial of awareness, because a true account of the brain requires it
Nothing about the brain, because an integrated person has no body
A ghost, brought in to perceive what the machine is not allowed to perceive
The reality of the body and of causal study. Drop the denial of awareness and the managed machine

feedback.note: Keep the body and the causal study, and drop the denial of awareness, because chemistry does not make the faculty a fiction. Managing a machine treats the person as the mindless device. Importing a ghost to do the perceiving returns the other half of the split instead of leaving the organism its faculty.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that rejects the mechanical caricature.

parts.text: The body is not a mindless

feedback.note: The body is not a mindless machine the mind must conquer, because the body is the living organism whose faculty awareness is. Organism, faculty, and person fail in the blank because those name what he is, not the caricature. Conquest is the war, and it has no second creature to win it.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle that states what the body is and what it is not.

feedback.note: The body is the living organism rather than a mindless machine, so awareness is not a tenant that must conquer it. A ghost's enemy would restore the war, and an illusion would deny the organism, because the body is real and conscious. Causal processes remain real. What fails is the claim that nobody is aware.

exercises.prompt: What is the life of an organism, understood as a kind of action?

choices.text: Self-generated action that sustains the organism
A static condition that continues without any action
An outside push, with no aim set by the organism itself
A purpose assigned later by someone who watches the motion

feedback.note: Life is self-generated, self-sustaining action, so the organism's own activity is what keeps it in existence. A static condition fails because a living thing that stops acting does not remain alive, and an outside push or a later label fails because neither is the organism acting to sustain itself.

exercises.prompt: A plant sends roots toward water. What makes that action goal-directed?

choices.text: A watcher later decides to call the growth a purpose
The plant's own action is organized to keep the plant alive
The water imposes a purpose the plant itself does not enact
Root and water are merely conjoined, and the plant's nature adds nothing

feedback.note: The plant generates action aimed at its own life, which is what goal-direction means for a living thing. A later label fails because a bystander's words do not create the goal, and constant conjunction fails because it drops the organism's nature as the source of the action.

exercises.prompt: Must an organism form concepts of its goal before the action can be goal-directed?

choices.text: No. The direction of the self-sustaining action is enough, as in a plant
Yes. Only a being that states a purpose in words can have a goal
Yes. Without concepts the action is a whim and has no relation to life
No. Every physical change is a goal, whether or not anything is alive

feedback.note: A plant's action is goal-directed without concepts, because the goal is the direction of the life-sustaining action, not a stated plan. Restricting goals to speakers fails because it erases plant and animal life, and spreading goals over every physical change fails because a rock is not sustaining itself.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the account of goal-direction that fits it.

pairs.right: Generates action aimed at its own life
Change that sustains no life
Self-generated, self-sustaining action

pairs.left: Action that has stopped for good
pairs.right: The end of that organism's life

feedback.note: Goal-direction belongs to living action aimed at the organism's continued life, not to a label or to a dead motion. Inanimate change fails as a goal because there is no life it is keeping in existence, and a stopped metabolism fails to leave a life behind because life was that action.

exercises.prompt: A river cuts a canyon across long ages. Which account fits the river?

choices.text: It is goal-directed, because every causal sequence is a purpose
It is goal-directed, because the canyon is the end the river chose
It changes, but it is not acting to sustain a life, so it has no goal
It is not causal at all, because only living things are able to act

feedback.note: The river's cutting is real causal change, and it is not a goal, because the river is not a living organism sustaining itself. Calling every causal sequence a purpose fails because it paints aims onto the inanimate, and denying causality outside life fails because identity still governs how lifeless things act.

exercises.prompt: If an organism's self-sustaining action stops and does not resume, what remains of its life?

choices.text: It remains alive in a quieter form, with the same goal stored unused
Death is only a name observers use, so the goal continues as a label
The goal becomes a wish that keeps the organism existing without action
Nothing of that life remains. Life was the action, and the organism is dead

feedback.note: Life is the self-sustaining action, so when that action ends for good the organism is dead rather than alive in storage. A quieter form fails because there is no life that outlasts the action, and a wish or a label fails because neither can keep an organism in existence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the principle that states what the life of an organism is.

feedback.note: Life is self-generated, self-sustaining action, so the blank names that action rather than a condition of doing nothing. Stillness fails because an organism that does not act does not stay alive, and a label or a decree fails because neither is the organism generating the action that sustains it.

exercises.prompt: Build the principle in the order that states what life is.
